access_points_caveat: This is a river/stream paddling-access layer from the Division of WATERCRAFT, not a Division of Wildlife fishing-access layer. There is no confirmed dedicated statewide fishing-access-point feed for Ohio (unlike Indiana's Fish_Access_RO or Michigan's boating-access FeatureServer). It does NOT cover lake/reservoir shoreline access or boat ramps on lakes -- only stream/river put-ins, portages, and dam locations. Many points are portage-around-a-dam markers, not fishing spots. Server caps queries at 1000 rows and exceeded that cap on an unfiltered pull during this Mode E pass, so a statewide count is unknown; always filter by county or waterbody name rather than pulling everything. ODNR also runs a 'Where to Fish' species-abundance dashboard (data.ohio.gov) and an 'Interactive Ohio Lake Fishing Map' (per-lake PDF maps at ohiodnr.gov/.../fishing-lake-maps) -- neither was confirmed as a queryable GPS/access-point API in this pass; the lake-maps page is PDF-per-lake, not a feed.

regulations_summary.smallmouth_bass: 5/day (singly or in combination with largemouth), 12 in minimum, statewide
regulations_summary.walleye_saugeye: 6/day (singly or in combination), no statewide minimum size
regulations_summary.northern_pike: not listed as a separate line in the statewide table in this pass -- treat as unconfirmed, don't assume unlimited

regulations_summary.blue_catfish: no limit under 35 in; 1/day (statewide) for 35 in and over
regulations_summary.flathead_catfish: no limit under 35 in; 1/day (statewide) for 35 in and over
regulations_summary.crappie: 30/day (singly or in combination, white/black crappie), no statewide minimum size
regulations_summary.bluegill_sunfish: no separate statewide limit found in this pass -- falls under general/'all other fish' catch-all; not independently confirmed

regulations_summary.trout_combined_inland: INLAND waters statewide (lakes, reservoirs, rivers, streams): 5/day, all trout species singly or in combination, NO minimum size. Ohio does not break inland trout out by species. SITE-SPECIFIC OVERRIDES that beat this default: Clear Creek (Fairfield Co. Rd 69 bridge to US 33 bridge, Hocking Co.) and Clear Fork of the Mohican River (Ashland Co.) = 2/day, no minimum; Mad River and tributaries and Clear Fork of the Mohican (Richland Co.) = 2/day, 12 in minimum. BROOK TROUT POSSESSION IS PROHIBITED entirely from the Ashtabula, Chagrin, Grand and Conneaut rivers and their tributaries.
regulations_summary.trout_and_salmon_lake_erie_zone: SEPARATE REGULATORY ZONE -- Lake Erie proper AND the entire length of every Lake Erie creek, river and tributary. Regulated as 'Trout & Salmon' combined on a SEASONAL schedule, not a flat rule: Mar 1 - May 15 = 2/day, no minimum; May 16 - Aug 31 = 5/day, 12 in minimum; Sep 1 - Feb 28 = 2/day, no minimum. Exception: Cold Creek upstream of State Route 2 (Erie Co.) = 5/day, no minimum, year-round (not date-tiered). Brook trout possession also prohibited in the Ashtabula/Chagrin/Grand/Conneaut systems under this table. Do NOT merge these numbers with the inland rule above -- different zone, different schedule.
regulations_summary.steelhead: Ohio NEVER uses 'steelhead' as a regulatory category in its size/bag tables. Steelhead is an anadromous rainbow trout, and is covered by whichever zone the water sits in: the Lake Erie 'Trout & Salmon' seasonal table if in Lake Erie or a tributary (which is where the runs are), or the inland 'Trout' line otherwise. The only place the word appears is the voluntary Fish Ohio trophy-award program (28 in qualifying length for Lake Erie) -- that is a recognition threshold, NOT a legal limit, and must never be quoted as one.
regulations_summary.rainbow_trout: See trout_combined_inland (and trout_and_salmon_lake_erie_zone if the water is Erie or a tributary).
regulations_summary.brook_trout: See trout_combined_inland, but note the outright POSSESSION PROHIBITION on the Ashtabula, Chagrin, Grand and Conneaut rivers and tributaries -- this is a total ban, not a limit.
regulations_summary.kokanee_salmon: NOT FOUND in Ohio's regulations -- not a species known to be established here. Do not infer a limit from the trout or the Lake Erie salmon rule.
water_specific_examples_found: Knox Lake: bass 5/day, 18 in minimum (overrides the 12 in statewide bass minimum)
Acton Lake and Findley Lake: bass split limit, 4/day total (2 fish under 15 in + 2 fish 15 in or longer)

closed_seasons.note: No closed season found anywhere in the 2026-27 regulations PDF for any species. This matches SKILL.md rule 4 (only Michigan has genuine statewide closed seasons for walleye/pike/musky among these five states) -- Ohio regulates by size/bag limit year-round, not by season.

license_summary.source: same PDF as regulations_source -- fees current for the 2026-27 season as fetched 2026-08-20, confirm before relying on them past this season
license_summary.where_to_buy: Three channels, per the official 2026-27 regulations guide p.4: at any authorized license sales agent statewide (locate via ODNR's 'Find a License Agent' map), inside the free official HuntFish OH mobile app (iOS/Android -- ODNR markets in-app purchase as a core function, not just an info app), and online. CAVEAT verified 2026-08-21: the regs guide names wildohio.gov as the online purchase domain, but that domain returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch; the confirmed-live storefront is oh-web.s3licensing.com/Home. Prefer the app or an in-person agent if the web route misbehaves, and re-check wildohio.gov before quoting it as the purchase link.

stocking_source: https://data.ohio.gov/wps/portal/gov/data/view/ohio-fish-stocking-records (dataset described as 1970-present, weekly updates, per ODNR's own referral page at ohiodnr.gov/buy-and-apply/hunting-fishing-boating/fishing-resources/fish-stocking-records) -- ODNR's referral page states no login is required, but the live data.ohio.gov dataset page itself displayed 'You must have an account, log in, and have access approval to view this data' when fetched in this pass. Data.ohio.gov's other ODNR fishing dashboards ('Where to Fish', 'Sport Fish Report') showed the same access-approval wall. Treat the stocking dataset as NOT confirmed publicly accessible without an account, despite ODNR's own marketing copy -- this directly contradicts this toolkit's own prior research note that flagged data.ohio.gov as having 'a strong stocking CSV.'
reciprocity: Ohio River main stem is reciprocal with Kentucky (per SKILL.md rule 5) -- confirm current terms directly before relying on it for a specific stretch.
great_lakes_note: Lake Erie shoreline is not covered by this file (per SKILL.md rule 7) -- Ohio has a separate Lake Erie fishing regulations/zoning layer that was not researched in this pass.

TROUT/STEELHEAD ADDED 2026-08-21 from the official 2026-27 Ohio Fishing Regulations PDF (dam.assets.ohio.gov ... /OhioFishingRegs_English.pdf, effective Mar 1 2026 - Feb 28 2027), pages 6-7 and 10-12 read directly rather than via a summary. Two things to carry forward: (1) Lake Erie and its tributaries are a genuinely separate zone with a seasonal schedule -- recorded here as its own entry, do not merge with inland; (2) NO CLOSED SEASON for trout, salmon or steelhead was found anywhere in the document, but the PDF disclaims itself as a summary and names the Ohio Administrative Code as authoritative, so this is 'not found', not a positive guarantee that none exists.
